meta.title: XROUT - the SINTRAN name and routing service
meta.purpose: How a name becomes an address, how a letter is forwarded, and the SEAT accounting that goes with it. The seat rule is here because getting it wrong costs nothing visible at the time and closes a service hours later.
meta.authority: This file and the C# must agree - the conformance tests assert the parts a machine can check.
meta.layering: XROUT requests ride as ordinary XMSG messages with the Route option set. See sintran-wire.json for the header.
meta.one_line: the name and routing service - and the seat count that decides if a service has room

status_values.MEASURED: Observed on the wire or against a live machine, with the evidence named.
status_values.INFERRED: Follows from something measured, or read from the ND manuals, but not itself observed here.
status_values.UNKNOWN: Copied or mirrored. Never computed or varied.
status_values.SUPERSEDED: Believed once, disproved. Kept so it is not re-derived.

the_seat_law.summary: XROUT holds a FREE-CONNECTION count for a registered connection port, forwards a letter only while it is above zero, and DECREMENTS IT ON FORWARD - before the receiver has seen a byte of the body.
the_seat_law.evidence: the real file access server builds its 30 seats this way, captured; and ChatSeatAccountingTests reproduces the whole rule

consequences.rule: The seat belongs to the ARRIVAL, never to a kind of message.
consequences.why: A letter carrying something other than the expected request, or a body too damaged to decode, never reaches a handler - so no handler can give the seat back. Settling seats per message kind leaks one every time.
consequences.found: 2026-08-11, by reading two independent implementations of one rule against each other

consequences.rule: Keep the seat only if the arrival put somebody NEW in the room.
consequences.why: 'Became a member', not 'was accepted': a member sending a second letter spends a second seat and only one of them is theirs.

consequences.rule: A leaked seat is invisible when it happens.
consequences.why: No error, no log line, nobody refused. The service is simply one seat smaller for ever, and it surfaces much later as XROUT turning requests away from a service that visibly has room.

marker.meaning: the ONLY thing telling a receiver that a seat was spent on this arrival
marker.evidence: both sample servers in the COSMOS Programmer Guide (ND-60.164.3) refuse anything that is not XMROU - 'IF MSGTYPE >< XMROU THEN' in PLANC and the same test in FORTRAN - and each then reads the CLIENT's magic from the arrived message to reply directly
marker.our_kernel: XFFWD produces XMROU via XmsgKernel.ChooseType, which tests Forward FIRST because XFHIP and XFRRO are the same bit

the_return.summary: A SEAT COMES BACK WHEN THE PORT IS CLOSED, not when a message is handled. XROUT marks the port with 5PKOC when it spends a seat; the XMSG kernel sees that bit on close and KICKS XROUT, which does the restoring. No XSNSP is sent and nothing crosses the wire.
the_return.evidence: XMSG-POFTABS-L03.SYMB, the port block definition, in ND's own words: 'SYMBOL 5PKOC=0  % KICK XROUT ON CLOSE (SET BY XROUT)' - bit 0 of the port status word XPSTA (word 1 of the port block). The kernel honours it in YCLOS=131306, the port-close routine: at ram:b30e 'BSKP ONE bit 0' on XPSTA, falling through to 'JPL [pool 0xb327]' = 0xb330 = 131460 = YKROU (kick XROUT) when the bit is SET, and skipping it when clear.
the_return.decode_cross_check: The BSKP bit field prints as bit<<3 and the sub-operation is ZRO below 0o200, ONE at or above. Three decodes in the same routine land on three DEFINED bits of XPSTA: fa 85 = 0o175205 -> bit 0 = 5PKOC; fa 75 = 0o175165 -> bit 14 = 5PIMX; fa ad = 0o175255 -> bit 5 = 5PKIK. (MAC numbers are octal, so the symbol file's 5PIMX=16 is bit 14 and 5PACT=17 is bit 15.)

xpsta_bits.name: 5PKOC
xpsta_bits.meaning: kick XROUT on close - SET BY XROUT when it spends a seat to deliver a connect letter
xpsta_bits.evidence: XMSG-POFTABS-L03.SYMB comment, and the test at YCLOS ram:b30e

xpsta_bits.name: 5PWAI
xpsta_bits.meaning: a receive-with-wait has been done on this port

xpsta_bits.name: 5PROU
xpsta_bits.meaning: this port is the routing port (XROUT)

xpsta_bits.name: 5PWAK
xpsta_bits.meaning: filling an empty message queue will cause a wake-up

xpsta_bits.name: 5PKIK
xpsta_bits.meaning: XROUT/COSROUT has been kicked (routing ports only)
xpsta_bits.evidence: XMSG-POFTABS-L03.SYMB comment, and a BSKP on it at YCLOS ram:b2ea

xpsta_bits.name: 5PIMX
xpsta_bits.meaning: immediate execution of code at XPIMC on a chain attempt
xpsta_bits.evidence: XMSG-POFTABS-L03.SYMB comment, and a BSKP on it at YCLOS ram:b2db

xpsta_bits.name: 5PACT
xpsta_bits.meaning: port active - YCLOS clears it at ram:b2d9
xpsta_bits.evidence: XMSG-POFTABS-L03.SYMB comment, and BSET ZRO bit 15 at YCLOS ram:b2d9

consequences.rule: A CLIENT of a connection port returns the seat by making the SERVER close its session port - which means finishing the conversation properly, not by sending anything seat-shaped.
consequences.why: The client cannot touch the counter; only XROUT can, and only the kernel can tell it to. The client's lever is the teardown message that makes the server conclude the session.
consequences.found: 2026-08-18, carving cos-fa-serv-e04.prog and then the XMSG kernel

consequences.rule: A SERVER that owns a connection port and does NOT close it per session must call XMPINFC (XSNSP) itself.
consequences.why: 5PKOC only fires on close. A long-lived server port that serves many sessions never closes, so nothing kicks XROUT and the count only ever falls. This is exactly the CHATSV case - it calls xmpinfc(0, myPort, 1, 0) - and it is why the FA server, which DOES close per session, needs no such call outside its initialisation.

consequences.rule: A leak can be several hops upstream of the counter.
consequences.why: Our FA client sent the server's own Close (07C0) instead of a client Release (0782). The server therefore never concluded the session, never closed the port, 5PKOC never fired and XROUT was never kicked. Three experiments aimed at the teardown frame's opcode and flags because the counter was the visible symptom; the fix was to make the server's close actually happen.

services.note: Service codes are DECIMAL here and octal in the ND manuals - the manual's XSRME=106 is 70. Mixing the two bases is an easy and silent error.

find_a_service_by_name.title: Reaching a service you only know by name
find_a_service_by_name.summary: The one thing XROUT is for, and where the seat is spent.
find_a_service_by_name.proved: every chat join and every FA connect in this repository

steps.note: at start-up: claim the name, and say how many callers can be held at once

steps.alt: the name is registered and has a free slot

steps.note: the free count DROPS HERE, before the server has seen the body
the server answers the client DIRECTLY - it learned the address from the arrival

steps.else: no such name, or it is full

else_steps.note: or XRNSP when the slots are all taken

steps.note: port to port; XROUT is not involved again
at shutdown: give the name back

gotchas.name: The slot is spent on FORWARD.
gotchas.detail: Not on acceptance. If the server does not seat the caller, IT must give the slot back - nobody else will.

gotchas.name: A leaked slot is silent.
gotchas.detail: The service just becomes one caller smaller, for ever, and refuses people hours later for no visible reason.
